configs.description: The unit as the dimensional drawing shows it. The rack brackets are in the box (data sheet). The 4G LTE modem needs an additional W4G part number (data sheet) and is not modelled.
configs.name: base

gaps.note: No photograph of any face is held; the only pictures of the product are angled marketing renders. Every position is read from the line drawing and every colour from a render.
gaps.wanted: A straight-on photograph of each face.

gaps.note: The documents name the lamps and state no colour or state for them; they are drawn as plain discs.
gaps.wanted: The maker's lamp table for the front panel.

gaps.note: The ears are not dimensioned: the holes are drawn (one round, one slotted) with no pitch.
gaps.wanted: A dimensioned drawing of the rack bracket.

gaps.note: The two rings marked MAIN and AUX are 'optional cell modem antenna mounts' (drawing). They are drawn as discs and are not ports.
gaps.wanted: The maker's drawing of the mounts, and which part numbers fit them.

gaps.note: The drawing shows the second Ethernet jack and the phone jack and says a label is added for units without them; the documents do not say whether a jack sits behind the label. Both are drawn as the drawing shows them.
gaps.wanted: Which part numbers carry the second Ethernet jack and the phone jack.

gaps.note: No held page shows the underside.
gaps.wanted: A drawing or photograph of the underside.

gaps.note: The drawing shows one side only, and no held page shows the other.
gaps.wanted: A drawing or photograph of the other side.

gaps.note: The drawing does not say which side its side view shows. It is drawn as the left, an estimate. Three hints point that way and none states it. The hardware guide puts the SIM card cover panel on the left hand side, adjacent to the cellular antenna. The guide says 'Side vents' in the plural. The side view stands below the top view and lines up with it as the file opens.
gaps.wanted: A drawing or photograph that names the side.

gaps.note: The drawing's top view also shows, beyond the cover's outline, the two ears edge on and ten rear bodies. The ten are two inlet bodies and eight outlet bodies. These are not drawn. A face is a width by height box (the view `size`, device schema lines 1352 to 1367). The kit has no shape for a part outside it.
gaps.wanted: A kit shape for a part beyond a face's box.

gaps.note: The side view's bottom edge is a rounded fold. It is not drawn. The `bevel` (device schema line 797) is a flat 45 degree cut. The `rounded` (line 820) rounds plan corners. So the kit has no rounded-fold shape.
gaps.wanted: A kit shape for a rounded fold along an edge.

gaps.note: The data sheet (page 2) prints '100/240V' for the -2 models and the inlet label on the drawing reads 100-240V, 50/60 Hz, 16A; the hardware guide (appendix A) prints '208 - 240 VAC'. The device states the data sheet's figure.
gaps.wanted: The maker's statement of the -2 input range.

chassis.note: Width 17.15 inches (435.6 mm) is the drawing's top cover width, and the drawing's 18.32 inches is the distance between the rack ear holes. The height is the data sheet's 1.75 inches, one rack unit and the drawing prints 1.74 (the guide and the data sheet agree with each other). The depth is 8.7 inches, the data sheet and the drawing; the hardware guide prints 8.75. No net weight is stated, only a shipping weight, so none is given.

colour.note: Median pixels of the angled render on the data sheet (page 2, 'CPM-1600-2-ECA'; the DSM data sheet's renders show the same dark face): the front face #373b3e, the rear plate #ebf5fb (lit and bluish in the render) with black printing. A MARKETING RENDER IS NOT A PHOTOGRAPH, AND NO HELD DOCUMENT HAS ONE, SO EVERY COLOUR HERE IS UNCHECKED AGAINST A PHOTOGRAPH. The red printed bars and the red logo block the render shows are not drawn.

ears.note: The drawing shows an ear at each end with two holes (one round, one slotted) and the data sheet says '19 Rack Brackets Included'. The ear hole pitch is not dimensioned; the drawing's 18.32 inches is the distance between the two ear hole axes. The ears are drawn at the faceplate, so the shipped position is flush.

inlets.note: IEC-320-C20 (hardware guide, section 2.2 and 2.5), '20 Amp' each (data sheet). A cord is not in the box for the -2 models: the data sheet lists the power cord as '(Sold Separately)', so none is drawn.

lamps.note: The lamps of both faces are drawn as plain discs, not as states: the hardware guide names them (port activity, plug activity or status) and does not state a colour or a state for any, so none is claimed.

method.note: THE DRAWING IS LINE ART AT ABOUT 1 TO 3 AND CARRIES NO CONNECTOR DIMENSION. Positions are measured on its vector geometry (a jack's outline, an outlet's box, an inlet's housing), centred on the drawn faceplate; a part is placed by its centre on the drawn outline. The drawn faceplate is slightly shorter than the stated height (drawing 1.74 or 3.46 inches against 1.75 or 3.5), so vertical positions are centred on the face. A lamp's spacing inside its frame is the drawing's. The captions inside the buttons, the lamp and port numerals, the ACT and LNK legends over the Ethernet jacks and the SETUP bracket over port 1 are placed from the printed positions in the drawing and are good to about 0.7 mm.

outlets.note: Data sheet page 2 and the drawing: eight IEC C13 outlets in one row, A1 to A8 (the drawing's 'SWITCHED OUTPUT RECEPTACLES IEC C13'); a divider after A4 and each inlet 'supplies power to a single four-outlet Bus' (hardware guide, section 2.5). The ATS models feed the same outlets from a primary and a secondary inlet (hardware guide); this device is the standard, non-ATS family. No breaker is stated.

power.note: Data sheet page 2: '100/240V' (footnote: 200/240V with the ATS add-on), '3.2/7.6 kW' of power distribution at 80% derating (the CPM-800-2 and CPM-1600-2 rows), 20 amps per inlet; the inlet label the drawing prints reads 100-240V, 50/60 Hz, 16A. The hardware guide (appendix A) prints 208 - 240 VAC for the -2 models and the data sheet and drawing do not; the device states the data sheet's figure and the disagreement is a gap. The unit's own draw is not stated by any held document, so no power-max-w is given.

serial-ports.note: RJ45 RS-232 serial ports, eight (hardware guide, 'Eight (8) RJ45 connectors'), port 1 marked SETUP. Units ship with a standard or a straight pinout and which a part number has is not stated (hardware guide, appendix B), so the jacks state the media and no pinout.

serial-role.note: The ports are console server ports (hardware guide, 'Serial Ports: connection to console ports on target devices').

sources.note: NO PHOTOGRAPH IS HELD. Every position on both faces is read from the vector figures of the maker's one-page dimensional drawing (CPM-800 family, revision A): the views carry no dimension for a connector, so each is a point of the drawing, converted at the scale that makes the drawn faceplate the 17.15 inches the drawing prints, and is good to about 1.5 mm. The hardware guide's front and back figures (CPM Series Hardware Guide figures 2.1 to 2.5; DSM Series Hardware Guide figures 2.1 to 2.6) agree with the drawing on the order of every connector. The colours are read from the angled renders on the data sheets, which are marketing renders and not photographs.

top-and-left.note: Source: CPM-800 dimensional drawing, one page: top view and the lower side view. The drawing carries no dimension for a screw or a slot. Positions are read from its vector figure at the scale that makes the drawn cover 17.15 inches wide, and are good to about one millimetre. Slot counts are counted twice on the 600 dpi page. The side is drawn as the left, which is an estimate.
